title: Completed integral pieces and the normalized localization comparison
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$, and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-pc-scheme]; noetherian means locally noetherian and quasi-compact, dimension is the supremum of lengths of strict chains of irreducible closed subsets, and invertibility means that $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring. On the fixed small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $B_T=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_T$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_T=B_T[1/\varpi]$. These are canonically the continuous-function ring sheaves $V\mapsto C(|V|,A)$ and $V\mapsto C(|V|,E)$, respectively, with constant-section coefficient maps [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. Modules and tensor products mean sheaf modules and sheaf tensor products [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. A continuous-constructible integral module has a finite locally closed stratification on which it is pro-etale locally $B_T\otimes_A P$ for a finitely presented $A$-module $P$ [def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module, def-constructible-stratification]. Let $v:V\hookrightarrow X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated open immersion and $t:S\hookrightarrow V$ a closed immersion whose complementary open is quasi-compact [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume $V$ and $S$ are also noetherian finite-dimensional with $\ell$ invertible. Identify their coefficient rings by the canonical immersion restrictions, and use the actual exact module functors of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. For every continuous-constructible $B_S$-module $N$, both $P=t_*N$ and $M=v_!P$ are continuous-constructible with finitely presented scalar models, allowing $0$ and torsion models. In the derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the degree-zero complexes $N[0]$, $P[0]$, and $M[0]$ belong respectively to $D^b_c(S,A)$, $D^b_c(V,A)$, and $D^b_c(X,A)$ [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete]. This includes derived completeness, uniformly bounded constructible reduction towers, and compatible etale-origin witnesses, with the completed coefficient rings just specified.

For a $B_T$-module $H$ set $\operatorname{loc}_T(H)=E_T\otimes_{B_T}H$. The canonical scalar comparisons are isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{loc}_V(t_*N)\xrightarrow{\sim}t_*\operatorname{loc}_S(N),\quad \operatorname{loc}_X(v_!P)\xrightarrow{\sim}v_!\operatorname{loc}_V(P),$$
and their composite is a natural isomorphism
$$c_N:\operatorname{loc}_X(v_!t_*N)\xrightarrow{\sim}v_!t_*\operatorname{loc}_S(N).$$
All three comparisons are normalized by the sequential localization colimit: for $n\geq0$ the stage map of $H\xrightarrow{\varpi}H\xrightarrow{\varpi}\cdots$ is $h\mapsto\varpi^{-n}\otimes h$, and after $t_*$ and $v_!$ its image is the same stage map with the same coefficient actions. In particular $c_N$ is the comparison induced by applying $v_!t_*$ to this colimit; it equals the composite of the separate open and closed comparisons, not just an unspecified isomorphism. For any specified isomorphism $\alpha:\operatorname{loc}_S(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}L$ of $E_S$-modules, its induced comparison with $v_!t_*L$ is exactly $(v_!t_*\alpha)\circ c_N$. For identity immersions this gives completed membership for every continuous-constructible integral sheaf on $X$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(2), Definition 6.8.10, Proposition 6.8.11(3), Lemma 6.8.13 and Remark 6.8.15, pp. 59-62

proof.text: Identify all immersion restrictions of $B$ and $E$ using [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction]. Take a finite stratification of $S$ witnessing continuous constructibility of $N$. For $P=t_*N$, use these same strata inside $V$, together with $V\setminus S$. Its restriction to $S$ is $N$ by $t^{-1}t_*\cong\mathrm{id}$, and its restriction to $V\setminus S$ is zero. For $M=v_!P$, use these strata inside $X$, together with the reduced closed complement $X\setminus V$. Its restriction to $V$ is $P$ by $v^{-1}v_!\cong\mathrm{id}$, and on the closed complement it is zero. All these identities are the module identities of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. The finite partitions are locally closed stratifications: a subset locally closed in a closed subset or an open subset is locally closed in the ambient space. On each old stratum the local model is exactly the original $B\otimes_A Q$; on each added stratum it is $B\otimes_A0$. Thus both sheaves are continuous-constructible, with the original finitely presented models and the finitely presented zero model. No torsion model is discarded.

For each $T=S,V,X$, the corresponding complex $N[0],P[0],M[0]$ is bounded with only the displayed module as its degree-zero cohomology. Step 1 and the hypothesis on $N$ give condition (iii) of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. Apply (iii)$\Rightarrow$(i) separately on these three schemes. The hypotheses are precisely the assumed noetherianity, finite dimension, invertibility of $\ell$, and the finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$; the completed ring is the same one by step 1. The conclusion includes derived completeness, one uniform finite cohomological window for the reductions, and compatible etale-origin witnesses, not merely constructibility of the underlying modules.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), using Proposition 6.6.11; the cited characterization explicitly retains the compatible etale-origin witnesses.

proof.text: For a module $H$ on any of these sites, apply [lem-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-module-colimit] with $R=B_T$, scalar ring $A$, and $t=\varpi$. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-tensor-comparison] its actual change of rings is the sheaf tensor $E_T\otimes_{B_T}H$, since [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficients-immersion-restriction] identifies $B_T[1/\varpi]$ with $E_T$. The cited colimit formula says exactly that its $n$th coprojection is $\lambda_{T,n}(h)=\varpi^{-n}\otimes h$. In particular $\lambda_{T,n+1}(\varpi h)=\lambda_{T,n}(h)$. This construction works for every module, including zero and modules killed by powers of $\varpi$.

The underlying space of the noetherian scheme $V$ has quasi-compact opens, hence quasi-compact intersections of affine opens; thus $V$ is qcqs. The small sequence indexed by $\mathbf N$ is filtered. Consequently [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] says that $t_*$ preserves the colimit in step 3. It preserves multiplication by $\varpi$, since its module action is through the canonical ring restriction of step 1. Restricting the $E_V$-module $t_*\operatorname{loc}_S(N)$ to $B_V$ gives the same module direct image as first restricting to $B_S$: both are base-change evaluation with the same restricted scalar action. Therefore the colimit comparison is an isomorphism $d_N:\operatorname{loc}_V(t_*N)\to t_*\operatorname{loc}_S(N)$, uniquely determined by $d_N\lambda_{V,n}=t_*\lambda_{S,n}$. It is the canonical scalar comparison: its zeroth-stage map is the direct image of the localization unit, and its $n$th-stage map is that map multiplied by $\varpi^{-n}$. It is $E_V$-linear, since it is $B_V$-linear and commutes with inverse multiplication by $\varpi$; local fractions generate the sheaf localization.

source.place: Tag 0738, sites.tex lemma-directed-colimits-sections, as incorporated in the filtered-colimit clause of the cited ringed open/closed lemma; Bhatt–Scholze Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: The adjunction $v_!\dashv v^{-1}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] makes $v_!$ preserve this colimit: maps from $v_!(\operatorname{colim}H_n)$ to $G$ correspond to maps from $\operatorname{colim}H_n$ to $v^{-1}G$, hence to compatible families of maps from $v_!H_n$ to $G$. The extension-by-zero presheaf in that same statement has its given module on objects factoring through $V$, and zero otherwise. Applying it before or after restricting $E$-scalars to $B$ gives the same presheaf and the same underlying module sheaf after sheafification; the scalar maps agree by step 1. It also sends multiplication by $\varpi$ to multiplication by $\varpi$. Thus step 3 gives an isomorphism $e_P:\operatorname{loc}_X(v_!P)\to v_!\operatorname{loc}_V(P)$ with $e_P\lambda_{X,n}=v_!\lambda_{V,n}$. As in step 4 it is $E_X$-linear and equals the canonical scalar comparison, because its zeroth-stage map is extension by zero of the localization unit and its other legs are its multiples by $\varpi^{-n}$.

source.place: Tag 03DI (lemma-extension-by-zero), its displayed presheaf and adjunction; Tags 03CY and 03EK.

proof.text: Define $c_N=(v_!d_N)\circ e_{t_*N}$. Steps 4 and 5 give, for every $n$, $c_N\lambda_{X,n}=v_!t_*\lambda_{S,n}$. The functor $v_!t_*$ preserves this colimit, by the two preservation arguments already given. The uniqueness part of the colimit universal property therefore identifies $c_N$ with its induced comparison, including every coefficient action. For a morphism $f:N\to N'$, the formula $\lambda_n f=\operatorname{loc}(f)\lambda_n$ follows directly from $\varpi^{-n}\otimes f(h)$. Precomposing the naturality square for $c$ with every coprojection now makes both sides equal, so that square commutes. Finally, for a specified $\alpha:\operatorname{loc}_S(N)\xrightarrow{\sim}L$, postcomposing the same leg formula with $v_!t_*\alpha$ gives exactly the required comparison with $v_!t_*L$, again by colimit uniqueness. Setting both immersions to identities in step 2 proves the final membership clause.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; elementary uniqueness for the sequential localization cocones constructed in steps 3–5.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q47-4bd07b2f6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and its 6 steps in full, every cited statement, and Bhatt–Scholze 1309.1198 pp. 59–62 (Def 6.8.10, Prop 6.8.11(3), Lemma 6.8.13, Rem 6.8.15). The delivery adds no new nodes. Statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are byte-identical to live. The item is still unsplit in live and side-live, so it is not superseded. The old mathlib_searches are kept and 5 searches are appended. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. There is no cycle, no SGA citation, and no re-split note on this item. The item carries old steps 5–7 of lem-per-rational-stratum-integral-models (compared with the Q145 7-step proof), and none of them is shortened. Step 1, adding zero strata, is correct and can count as elementary: ringed-open-closed gives i^{-1}i_*≅id and j^{-1}i_*=0. The coefficient-restriction isos make the ringed inverse image agree with the plain one. The strata stay locally closed. Advisory: it re-derives lem-weil-pbc-integral-model-open-closed-pieces instead of citing it, which is acceptable because that node's isomorphisms are unspecified. Step 2: (iii)⇒(i) of the stratified characterization gives D^b_c with completeness, the bounded tower and étale witnesses. Its hypotheses are assumed on S, V and X. Step 3: the scalar-localization colimit gives c_n β = η∘ϖ^{-n}, and extension-tensor-comparison identifies the change of rings with the sheaf tensor. Step 4: V is noetherian, hence qcqs, so t_* preserves filtered colimits. Step 5: v_! ⊣ v^{-1}. Step 6: colimit uniqueness gives the composite, naturality and the α formula. Edge cases checked: empty schemes, N=0, ϖ-torsion N, rank one, identity immersions, nonreduced S. I accept the 5 tool uses as generic tools of sk-thm-properbasechange. No changes.
